title: Human Dignity
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Human dignity means that every person possesses God-given worth that must be honored. Human value is not created by ability, health, status, usefulness, wealth, age, productivity, or social approval.
summary: Human dignity means that every person possesses God-given worth that must be honored. Human value is not created by ability, health, status, usefulness, wealth, age, productivity, or social approval.
christFocus: Jesus Christ dignifies the lowly by taking on human flesh, drawing near to the overlooked, and redeeming sinners by His blood. In Him, God restores people who have been degraded by sin, shame, and rejection.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Human dignity is rooted in creation. Every person bears God’s image and must be treated with honor. This dignity does not rise and fall with strength, independence, intelligence, beauty, social usefulness, or public success.

Sin leads people to rank others by power, money, appearance, race, class, ability, or reputation. Scripture confronts partiality and calls God’s people to honor the poor, weak, vulnerable, and overlooked.

Jesus repeatedly moved toward people others dismissed. He received sinners, touched the unclean, welcomed the weak, and sought the lost. His ministry reveals that God does not measure worth by the standards of prideful society.

Human dignity does not deny sin or remove the need for repentance. Rather, it declares that sinners are valuable creatures who need redemption, not disposable problems to ignore or despise.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People who have been rejected, abused, disabled, impoverished, addicted, aged, or overlooked may begin to believe they are less valuable. Scripture speaks a stronger word: dignity comes from God.

This doctrine also rebukes contempt. God’s people cannot claim to love Him while despising those made in His image. Human dignity must shape ministry, discipleship, justice, mercy, speech, and care for the vulnerable.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Treat every person as one who matters before God. Reject favoritism, contempt, and usefulness-based love. Honor the weak, protect the vulnerable, speak with dignity, and let Christ teach you to see people through creation and redemption rather than worldly status.
